title.en: Detail inset with a persistent context anchor

summary: Enlarge a feature in a secondary view while retaining its identity, position and orientation in the overview.
objective: Open a close-up inset for a small feature and keep an overview anchor that follows the same feature during camera and state changes.
intent_signals: Open a close-up inset for a small feature and keep an overview anchor that follows the same feature during camera and state changes.
example_prompts: Open a close-up inset for a small feature and keep an overview anchor that follows the same feature during camera and state changes.

principles: Use an inset when a small feature needs magnification while the whole remains relevant; the design rationale is reduced back-and-forth camera travel, not a measured usability claim.
Keep an explicit relationship between the inset subject and overview anchor. Enlargement and changed lighting are presentation choices and must not imply a different physical scale or material.
implementation: Track a stable feature ID plus its model-space anchor and bounds. Derive the overview marker from the main camera and fit a separate detail camera to the same feature; do not clone independent mutable model state.
Label orientation and relative scale where they matter. If a diagrammatic inset rotates, clips or explodes the feature, disclose that transform and retain a return-to-assembled control.

Clip the connector to its viewport, and distinguish an off-screen anchor from a visible one. Avoid drawing a connector through an unrelated object as if it were an attachment. Reposition the panel when it obscures the inspection target.

Provide close, refocus and keyboard/list alternatives. Closing the inset restores any temporarily hidden content and leaves main camera and simulation state unchanged unless a documented focus action changed them.
observable_checks: Open an inset, rotate the overview and advance one explicit state step: both views identify the same feature and time sample.
Move the anchor off screen or occlude it: the marker reports that condition rather than jumping to a different visible object.
Resize the viewport, switch selected features and close the inset; no stale connector, duplicated state or hidden main-view geometry remains.

known_limits: An inset can expose detail only present in the source geometry or data. It does not add verified internal structure or increase source resolution.
Draft authored guidance; no renderer, interaction artifact or scientific result was executed for this record.
creative_affordances: Choose layout and visual emphasis to support the stated inspection task; these are design proposals rather than proven usability improvements.
